title: Browse Papyrus record types without collapsing them into stories
description:
Feature: Type-aware Papyrus record browsing
Scenario: See all actual base record models
Given the current Papyrus schema
When I browse records by domain, type, or text
Then every persistent base model is discoverable with meaningful labels and actual schema fields
And synthetic examples disclose that no live backend mapping is connected
Scenario: Reference curation lifecycle
Given a synthetic reference with an actual curation status
When I change its curation status and reload
Then the local preview store preserves the status and reason
Scenario: Non-workflow records
Given an attachment, relationship, identity, or publication copy
When I open its list and detail
Then no story stage controls or invented workflow is presented
And the original story board and priming remain functional

comments.author: home
comments.text: Approved direction and compatibility checkpoint: Papyrus newsprint (not green/cobalt/Prospectus); distinct Story, Assignment and Reference boards, forum MessageThread/Message, all schema types discoverable as explicitly synthetic partial examples. Actual old ten-section nav inventoried; carry-forward action flows remain separate work, no full parity claim. Story→Article direction approved, but Kanbus validator fixes canonical hierarchy and non-hierarchy story cannot parent. Preserve Item revisions and Assignment identities; propose explicit typed cross-model links rather than false parentage; no hierarchy change/migration applied. See docs/unified-records-review.md.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Local increment a26de81 is now served on the same 8899 URL. Actual Papyrus paper/ink/rule tokens and self-hosted Playfair/Jakarta replace green/retro styling. Three separate board-capable types (existing actual Kanbus stories, schema-shaped local Assignment and Reference adapters), persistent forum thread replies, and schema-type lists/linked details are verified. Seven Python tests, TypeScript, lint/build, original Kanbus+Cyclotron browser workflows and new 390/1440 light/dark type-aware browser suite pass. Existing ten-section directory is carried forward with explicit missing-action labels; this is NOT old-CMS feature parity or cloud implementation of 39 models. No production changes or hierarchy migration. See docs/unified-records-review.md.
